definition: Gavin! Almost 3 years old, Renata and Lenin's adorable son is often found playing in the acabowl. Feel free to join him and enjoy a study break.
The Wiess courtyard/quad. The social epicenter of Wiess, which frequently features people hanging out, playing soccer, and studying.
Giant covered swinging picnic table of glory, in the Acabowl.
A grill, in the Acabowl.
The terrace behind the Upper Commons that we share with Hanszen.
A trampoline, in the Acabowl.
Formal dinner held in the commons once a semester to honor Wiess Associates. Every college has their own.
The Fourth Floor balcony. Great spot to hang out or watch the sunset.
The area under the Commons used for storage and shirt screen making. Can be accessed using your room key.
Wiess Aca-children, son and daughter of the Byrds, who love jumping on the trampoline and reading.
Event held for the new students after they ace their first round of exams.
Former Wiess RAs, and some of the best people you may ever meet.
Governing body of Wiess. Made up entirely of Wiessmen. Meets every other Wednesday at 10pm in the Upper Commons. There's always free food.
The place to be. You will eat here, study here, act here, play here, party here, hang out here, and well, live here.
An honorary title conferred upon one deserving upperclassman and one freshman each Hallowen.

A day filled with college bonding, hanging out, a nice dinner, and an evening of entertainment. Wiess' is always held the last day of classes each semester. Each college has their own college night, which are not always on the last day of classes.
To pull up an extra chair at the corner of a table. Frequently occurs during meals but never at formal occasions.
Former Wiess RA’s and Wiessmen (Class of 2001). Awesome associates that you will constantly hear talking about “when Wiess was cool.”

The Man. The Legend. Ex-Wiess RA who started the Dr. Bill Grant program at Wiess, shirt screening, and whose section in Fondren Library includes every college theatre production during his time at Rice.
Wiess Master and History Professor. Starting off his fourth year as Wiess Master, he can't wait to get to know you!
Our new fourth floor RA. Assistant professor of Materials Science & Nanoengineering and Chemistry. Her many interests include running, traveling, and foreign lanugages.
Our college coordinator. If you need to know anything about anything, he’s the one to ask. He’ll always have a useful and slightly sassy answer, usually delivered in a bowtie.
Peer advisors for new students of Wiess College. They are awesome! Some colleges may confuse you by calling them “advisors.”
1. A 24-hour film marathon held during Dead Days. 2. The best way to waste time when you should be studying.
Rooms in the corner of Wiess that each hold five people.
First Tabletop production of the year, which includes, you guessed it, one-acts featuring new students.
Four hours of required service to Wiess. Necessary to enter the housing jack at the end of your first year. There are plenty of opportunities to get them!
Affectionate name for the Wiess powderpuff football team.
Event held for the new students after they ace their first round of exams.
Assistants to the Head Fellows during O-Week. Three people you should definitely get to know!
Organizers of O-Week and friends to all the new Wiessmen. Aka Victoria and Ryan.
Third floor RA. Be sure to stop by to chat about scuba diving and get to know him. Married to Renata and proud father of Gavin.
Former Wiess Masters and generally amazing people. Mike is a biology professor and loves to talk about Wiess history and traditions. Denise is a dog enthusiast and lover of arts and bargain shopping.
Wiess Master and elementary school principal. Loves being active and getting to know you.
The biggest party at Rice. Held at Wiess on the last Saturday of October, it features interesting decorations and creative costumes.
Off-campus Lounge. Hang out room for all the off-campus people.
Private dining room. A smaller room attached to the Commons.
The spreading of Halloween cheer, led by the College Idiots. Features Halloween songs, candles, and a visit to the other colleges.
The process used to assign rooms for the next year.
Contrary to popular belief, not much cooking goes on here. Fun place to hang out on Thursday evenings.
Where you get your food before you go sit down in the commons. We share one with Hanszen.
The hidden room on the fourth floor, adorned with goldenrod paint, comfortable couches, poker setups, and a karaoke machine.
The loud speakers that can be heard throughout the Acabowl on Friday afternoons or special occasions.
Weekend retreat to discuss Wiess issues and bond on a boat.
Wiess theater productions, held in the Wiess commons.
The newly renovated kitchen on the third floor. A great place to bake or cook for those Saturday nights when the servery is closed.
Held during the spring, Wiess hangs out in the Acabowl all day to eat good food and participate in various fun activities.
The most powerful cheer on campus, and the embodiment of everything that makes Wiess College cool.
An abbreviation of Team Wiess. Includes a little emphasis. Family, right?
Party to celebrate the new Cabinet held at Willy’ Pub each year.
1. An awesome room on the fourth floor, featuring a big projector and surround sound. 2. Site of Filmfest and open for use at any time, just make sure you get a room reservation!
A unique Wiess celebration of life. If you have any questions, just ask a friendly Wiessmen.
2nd floor of the commons. Has a pool table, ping pong table, TV, and lots of couches.
Wiess mascot, embodied by the giant wooden pig built by the Class of 2012 for Beer Bike. The pig will roll!
The Byrd's house. Where everybody knows your name, and the door is always open.
The inclusive, gender neutral term for the women and men of Wiess College. This includes you.
The official Wiess color. It will soon dominate your wardrobe. Remember it's not yellow!
Third floor RA and Bioengineering lecturer. Loves to talk and make delicious Mexican food. Married to Lenin, proud mama of Gavin. Also a shirt-screening expert!
Three big slabs of rock in the Engineering Quad.
Party held at Sid Rich college that brings back both awesome music and clothing.
A person majoring in humanities or social sciences.
The central academic quadrangle around Willy’s Statue.
A student majoring in architecture.
Alternative Spring Break; service project over spring break, often in another state.
Faculty, staff, or community members associated with a college. Darned good people to know.
Gym in Tudor Fieldhouse where the Rice basketball team plays.
The humorous last page of the Thresher.
A resident of Baker College.

An organization whose sole function is to undress, smear shaving cream on their bodies, and run around campus leaving a slimy trail of body prints. A favorite target of Wiessmen with buckets of water.

A competitive intercollege race held in the spring in which ten bikers and ten chuggers from each college compete in a struggle for personal and college pride. Also includes a water balloon fight and much rejoicing.
A term to describe the “real word” outside of Rice.
Classes frequently taken by freshmen science and engineering majors: Physics, Chemistry, and Calculus.
A modernistic glass building located behind Fondren. Home to Salento (a non-student operated coffeeshop) and is a great place to relax and sit outside.
A resident of Brown College.
1. The bell tower in the Engineering quad. 2. Rice’s yearbook 3. An undergraduate orchestras.
Collection of offices adjacent to the Student Center.
Student-run shop in the Student Center that provides caffeine to needy students. Also a great place to study and/or pretend to be a hipster.
The faculty dining club near Sewall Hall. Eat here if you get a chance.

Refers to distribution credits, Rice's way of making sure you get a balanced education. 12 credit hours of each category are required to graduate. D1 = humanities, D2 = social sciences, D3 = science and engineering.
The Digital Media Center. Lots of computers to use and cool equipment to check out.
A resident of Duncan College.
Fall formal. A major part of homecoming weekend and lots of fun!
The Rice library. It has seminar rooms, study rooms, and classrooms. Open 24 hours a day during the week.
Graduate Student Association.
Housing and Dining. Administrative office in charge of all food service and residential buildings on campus.
A resident of Hanszen College.
Extensive botanical growth that surrounds campus and the Academic Quad.
A student-run late night food stop for hungry students located at West and South Serveries. Accepts tetra.
Intramural. Informal, low-stress sports played among students. Not to be confused with college sports which are played between teams representing each of the colleges.
One-way road that loops around the center of campus.
Someone who bikes and chugs at Beer Bike.
A prank pulled on another college.
The online Rice radio station, run by students. Plays everything from jazz, to reggae, to bands you probably didn't think existed.
David Leebron - President of the University. Married to Ping.. Also sends fascinating holiday e-card every year.
A resident of Martel College.
Ceremony held during O-Week to officially welcome you to Rice.
The university computer/IT center. If you have problems with your computer, the people here are glad to help out. Also a great place to print large posters
A resident of McMurtry College.
Officially called First Look, a book with a catalogue of pictures of all incoming students.
The Marching Owl Band. That doesn’t march. They always put on an entertaining show during halftime, filled with amusing skits, jibes at opposing teams, and zany antics.
A student majoring in music.
Off campus. A.k.a. your sophomore year.
A 3-mile long path that encircles campus. Great for a jog or random people watching.
Pass/fail. There are many rules you'll learn about regarding P/F classes, but they can be lifesavers.
The Philharmonics, the largest acapella group on campus that holds performances throughout the year.
Willy’s Pub, located in the basement of the RMC (see below). Great place to grab a pizza and hang out with people across campus. Heavily populated on Thursday nights.
Party thrown by a residential college. Most colleges throw one per semester. All are themed.
A member of Jones college.
A resident of Lovett College
Mid-semester grades given to new students in the fall.
An independent literary magazine published entirely by students
Campus convenience store in the RMC.
Rice students that are trained as EMTs. Respond to emergencies on campus.
Only campus theater group not associated with a college.
Rice Memorial Center, also referred to as the Student Center. This is where you can find the bookstore, the convenience store, Coffeehouse, Pub, and important offices like Academic Advising.
Rice Program Council. The organization in charge of all university-wide events, like Beer Bike, Screw Yer Roommate, Ezperanza, and study breaks during finals.
Student Association. The campus-wide body representing students. Deals with campus-wide issues and administrative business.
The big archway in Lovett Hall. Tradition holds that if you walk through it between matriculation and graduation, you won't graduate.
The Rice mascot.
A student majoring in science or engineering.
A resident of Sid Richardson College.
Student Maintenance Representative. The liaison between H&D and the students. They can help you change the height of your bed or change your light bulbs.
Spontaneous Combustion, the improv skit group on campus. Check out one of their shows, they’re very funny!
Creatures seen throughout campus. Known to be very crazy and totally unafraid of humans.
Taco Cabana. A twenty-four hour food-serving institution and an all-nighter’s best friend.
Credit on your meal plan used to buy food at the RMC or the Hoot.
Rice’s student-operated newspaper. Check out the Backpage for some ol’ time ribbing, hehehe.
The frisbee-lacrosse-soccer amalgam frequently played on campus.
The other on-campus pub, often populated by grad students, but a great place for cheap beer.
The shopping center west of campus. Has lots of great restaurants and shops, all within walking distance!
A 24-hour restaurant to get a burger or legendary Honey Butter Chicken Biscuit. Ask for Texas Toast—it’s the only way to truly eat a Whataburger.
Your home and family.
A resident of Will Rice College
The week preceding Beer Bike, filled with college activities, alumni, and jacks.
A two-ton brass likeness of the founder of the university located in the center of the Academic Quad.
Southern slang short for "you all." Something you have to get used to. Y'all will be saying this if you want to or not.
